headline: High-risk shared Repl filesystem and shell access make prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts plausible; Superset’s allowlisted egress limits but does not remove pairwise risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and run shell commands, while Superset exposes API-driven data workflows and allowlisted egress. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could let attacker-controlled content in one agent influence the other. The pathway is plausible in default Repl usage, though not proven by docs for this exact pair.
conditions: IF both agents exchange files through the same Repl workspace
IF Superset ingests content produced by Replit Agent without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Require manual review of any file passed between agents
Strip instructions from imported text before parsing
Use provenance labels on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing handoff middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and can read/write the Repl filesystem; Superset can call APIs and has network egress, so sensitive workspace data could be exposed if artifacts are transferred into Superset or its connected data sources. The pair creates a realistic exfiltration path, and uncertainty about the exact integration should be resolved upward.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configuration from Replit workspace are copied into Superset inputs
IF Superset queries external systems containing the same sensitive data class
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Use a redacted export for any handoff
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on agent handoffs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has unrestricted shell, filesystem write, and git-state modification in a persistent Repl; Superset can also make API calls and network requests. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is enough to treat as dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF either agent writes while the other is editing or deploying
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Pause one agent before the other edits
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can generate code, configs, and deployment changes, and Superset can consume API-backed data workflows. If Superset treats Replit-produced artifacts as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification controls here, but the blast radius is more bounded than direct action-taking.
conditions: IF Superset uses Replit-generated files or SQL without validation
IF Replit output is promoted into dashboards or pipelines as-is
mitigations: Require a human review step before import
Validate schemas and SQL before execution
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Superset is a separate analytics system with allowlisted egress. If regulated data or secrets are moved from Replit into Superset, retention and residency obligations may diverge. Only the Replit side is clearly implicated, so the other agent is cited for the transfer path.
conditions: IF regulated data from Replit is loaded into Superset datasets
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before sharing
Avoid moving PHI or EU PII into Superset
Document retention settings in both systems
Limit Replit secrets exposure to non-regulated data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
